headline: Dry, steadily milder weather lasts through Saturday, then a coastal storm could bring 1–2 inches of rain or more and gusty winds late Sunday into Monday, though its track is still very uncertain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Strong high pressure keeps New York City and the surrounding area dry and clear Wednesday, with light winds mostly from the west-southwest to west-northwest at about 6–12 mph, possibly turning more southwesterly by mid to late afternoon. Wednesday night stays clear and calm, so how cold it gets will depend on how efficiently the ground cools off overnight, with outlying spots likely colder than the city.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday through Saturday stay dry as the high pressure slowly settles over the area, and temperatures keep warming, with highs reaching the upper 50s to mid 60s by Friday. Thursday morning is another chilly start under clear skies and light winds, but starting Thursday night a southwest breeze brings in a little more moisture, so lows won't drop as far into the weekend.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A well-developed storm is likely to form off the Southeast coast this weekend and then head northeast. If it tracks close enough, rain would spread up the coast late Sunday and continue through Monday, with 1–2 inches possible and locally more, plus gusts of 30–40 mph in parts of the area; the chance of rain is currently 30–60%. The American model and its AI version show this direct hit, while the European model keeps the storm farther out to sea with little or no impact, and rain totals could drop off sharply on the storm's western edge.

coast: Calm boating conditions through Saturday with no advisories: winds mostly from the northwest to west under 15 knots (about 17 mph) and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 feet. Seas start building Sunday, and a Small Craft Advisory may be needed by Sunday night if the storm comes close.
watch_for: Whether the Sunday–Monday storm tracks close to the coast (1–2+ inches of rain and 30–40 mph gusts) or stays offshore and mostly misses.
Where the sharp western edge of the rain sets up, which could mean big differences in totals over short distances.
confidence: High confidence in dry, gradually warming weather through Saturday; low confidence in the track, timing and rain totals for the late Sunday–Monday storm.
